stories.headline: Ukraine escalates deep strikes on Russian oil infrastructure and shadow fleet tankers
stories.summary: Ukraine launched an intensive wave of drone and maritime strikes against Russian energy export infrastructure over the week, hitting the Black Sea port and refinery at Tuapse four times in 16 days, a Baltic oil terminal at Primorsk, oil facilities in Perm and Orsk over 1,500 km from Ukraine's border, and multiple shadow fleet tankers near Novorossiysk and Primorsk. Zelensky confirmed strikes on a Karakurt-class cruise missile carrier, a patrol boat, and at least three shadow tankers on May 3, while threatening continued escalation if Russia does not halt its invasion.

stories.headline: Putin proposes May 9 Victory Day ceasefire via Trump; Zelensky rejects as 'manipulation'
stories.summary: After a phone call between Trump and Putin in which Putin proposed a brief ceasefire around Russia's Victory Day on May 9, Zelensky demanded clarification from Washington on whether the proposal amounted to more than 'a few hours of security for a parade in Moscow,' calling it manipulative theater. The Kremlin declared the ceasefire would proceed regardless of Kyiv's response, while Zelensky also warned Russia may seek sanctions relief as part of any truce deal. Ukraine's Foreign Minister Sybiha echoed the rejection, calling the proposal a 'crude diplomatic maneuver.'

stories.headline: Syrskyi orders mandatory two-month frontline rotation cap for Ukrainian troops
stories.summary: Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi signed an order on April 30 mandating that troops on frontline positions serve no longer than two months before mandatory rotation within the following month, with required medical examinations and guaranteed supplies. The order comes after viral images of emaciated soldiers from the 14th Mechanized Brigade sparked public outcry over troops reportedly serving over 500 consecutive days in combat positions; Syrskyi cited drone-dominated warfare as fundamentally changing logistics requirements.

stories.headline: Ukraine-Israel diplomatic row over stolen grain ship resolved as vessel leaves Haifa without unloading
stories.summary: A diplomatic confrontation between Ukraine and Israel escalated after the vessel Panormitis docked at Haifa carrying grain Kyiv says was stolen from Russian-occupied Ukrainian territory. Foreign Minister Sybiha formally requested Israel seize the vessel and threatened sanctions, sparking a public spat with Israeli FM Sa'ar who accused Kyiv of 'Twitter diplomacy.' The ship ultimately departed without unloading after Israeli importer Zenziper refused the cargo; Sybiha called it 'a clear signal' while Zelensky announced a broader campaign against Russia's shadow grain fleet.

stories.headline: Zelensky attends European Political Community summit in Yerevan, meets UK, Czech, Norwegian, Finnish leaders
stories.summary: President Zelensky traveled to Yerevan, Armenia on May 3 for the European Political Community summit, marking his first visit to the country. On the sidelines he met with UK Prime Minister Starmer, Czech PM Babiš, Norwegian PM Store, and Finnish PM Orpo, discussing military support, drone cooperation deals, and Ukraine's EU integration path. A social media moment went viral when Zelensky quipped to Starmer that he had arrived without a delegation.

stories.headline: Zelensky announces systemic military reform: pay hikes, contract terms, phased demobilization for June launch
stories.summary: President Zelensky on May 1 announced a comprehensive reform of Ukraine's armed forces, including significant pay increases for infantry and rear-area personnel, a new contract service system with defined terms, and a phased discharge mechanism for the longest-serving mobilized soldiers. Defense Minister Fedorov described the changes as 'systemic'; implementation is set to begin in June 2026 with Zelensky requesting a detailed action plan the following week.

stories.headline: NBU holds benchmark rate at 15%, cuts 2026 GDP forecast to 1.3% as war and Iran conflict fuel inflation
stories.summary: Ukraine's National Bank held its key interest rate at 15% at its April 30 monetary policy meeting and revised its 2026 GDP growth forecast down to 1.3% from 1.8%, citing a weak first quarter, ongoing energy grid damage from Russian strikes, and inflationary spillover from the Iran-Israel war via higher global oil prices. Inflation is now projected to reach 9.4% in 2026 before returning toward the 5% target in 2028. The NBU also noted it plans to hold the rate through Q2 2027.

The loan, approved by the EU last month, is designed to cover two-thirds of Ukraine's funding needs for two years, primarily for military spending.

stories.summary: Foreign Minister Sybiha condemned the Venice Biennale's decision to allow Russia to participate in its 2026 exhibition, calling it 'cowardly.' The entire jury subsequently resigned over the matter, which Sybiha framed as demonstrating 'consequences of decisions taken by leading international art platforms.' Italy's culture minister also boycotted. Ukraine also sent an origami deer sculpture to the Biennale as a symbol of resistance.
